--- title: "Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: AI in Your Workflow" subtitle: "
Bioinformatics Resource Center - Rockefeller University" author: - "[http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/](http://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/responsible_use_of_AI_for_noncoders/)" - "[brc@rockefeller.edu](mailto:brc@rockefeller.edu)" --- ::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"} # Responsible Use of AI for Non-Coders: AI in Your Workflow ::: ## Overview *Presenter: Matt — 50 mins* - [What is a good workflow](#what-is-a-good-workflow) - [Hard lines](#hard-lines) - [Controlling what is allowed](#controlling-what-is-allowed) # Good workflows {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## What is a good workflow ??What a good AI-assisted workflow looks like, framed for people who can't read the code the AI writes?? ## When you can't read the code ??How to check work you can't read line by line: ask for explanations, check outputs against known answers, test on small examples?? ## Environments and resources ??Which Python / R is being used, software environments, not using compute or data resources it shouldn't?? ## Good practice still applies Good coding practice is still essential when an AI writes the code: - Clear, specific instructions - Working on small subsets of data before the full dataset - ??Keeping a record of what was asked and done (messages, version control)?? # Hard lines {background-color="#23373B" .center .middle} ## CLAUDE.md and other configuration files ??What CLAUDE.md and similar instruction files are, and how to write them: be specific, set the tone you want?? ## Why rules loosen over time ??Why instructions can weaken over a long session (context compression), and how to guard against it?? ## Controlling what is allowed ??Permission settings, approval prompts, and how to restrict what the AI is allowed to do??
